subject.title: Cron jobs stall during AI model calls (model_call:stream_progress never completes)

question: Should this issue stay open as the tracker for the remaining `cron.wake` mode-now result-contract gap, or should maintainers split that gap into a focused issue and close this bundle after linking the implemented stream-stall fix?
rationale: The headline bug is fixed on main, but the remaining behavior is an API/product contract decision about accepted-versus-completed wake semantics and this issue bundles several cron failure modes.

options.title: Split the wake-result gap
options.body: Create or designate a focused tracker for `cron.wake` mode-now result reporting, then close this bundled issue once the split is linked and the current-main stream-stall fix is cited.

options.title: Keep this scoped to Bug 3
options.body: Leave this issue open only for the `cron.wake` mode-now accepted-then-failed behavior and ignore the already-fixed stream-stall headline for future triage.

options.title: Close after linked wake fixes land
options.body: Wait for the overlapping main-session wake candidates to land, then reassess whether they also cover the manual `cron.wake` result contract.

recommendation.title: Split the wake-result gap
recommendation.body: Create or designate a focused tracker for `cron.wake` mode-now result reporting, then close this bundled issue once the split is linked and the current-main stream-stall fix is cited.

likelyOwner.reason: Current main blame points to Peter on the relevant cron/wake files, and the remaining decision is a cron API contract boundary rather than only the merged run-lifecycle stack.
